name: Uttarakhand
blurb: The high Himalayan headwaters of the Ganga, Uttarakhand's Char Dham pilgrimage circuit includes some of Hinduism's most physically demanding sacred sites.

districts.name: Rudraprayag
districts.blurb: A mountainous district at the confluence of the Alaknanda and Mandakini rivers, gateway to Kedarnath.

places.name: Kedarnath Temple
places.blurb: One of the twelve Jyotirlingas, a stone temple at over 3,500 metres reachable only on foot, pony or helicopter, that famously survived the devastating 2013 floods largely intact.
places.bestPhoto: The temple against snow peaks in early morning light
places.history: One of the twelve Jyotirlingas and part of the Char Dham pilgrimage circuit, the present stone temple is traditionally attributed to the 8th-century philosopher Adi Shankaracharya, built on a much older site of worship. The temple famously survived largely intact during the devastating 2013 Uttarakhand floods, when a large boulder is credited with diverting floodwaters around the main structure.
places.architecture: A robust stone structure built from massive interlocked grey stone slabs, in a simple, sturdy style suited to its high-altitude Himalayan setting at over 3,500 metres, fronted by a large statue of Nandi the bull.

timeline.label: Present stone temple built, traditionally attributed to Adi Shankaracharya.
Catastrophic Uttarakhand floods devastate the surrounding town; the temple structure itself survives largely intact.

facts: One of the twelve Jyotirlingas and part of the Char Dham Yatra pilgrimage circuit.
Only accessible on foot or by helicopter — no road reaches the temple directly.
Closed for roughly six months each winter due to heavy snow, with the deity ceremonially moved to Ukhimath.
